name: DirichletCharacter
IsPrimitive
result.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → DirichletCharacter R n → Prop
result.informal_description: A Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $n$ is primitive if its conductor equals the modulus $n$, i.e., the smallest natural number $d$ such that $\chi$ factors through the projection $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ is exactly $n$ itself.

name: DirichletCharacter
primitiveCharacter
result.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → (χ : DirichletCharacter R n) → DirichletCharacter R χ.conductor
result.informal_description: For any Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $n$ with values in a commutative monoid with zero $R$, the primitive Dirichlet character associated to $\chi$ is the unique character $\chi_0$ modulo the conductor $d$ of $\chi$ such that $\chi$ equals the composition of $\chi_0$ with the canonical projection $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$.

name: DirichletCharacter
isPritive_one_level_zero
result.informal_description: The Dirichlet character modulo 1 is primitive, as its conductor equals the modulus 1.

name: DirichletCharacter
primitive_mul
result.signature: {m : ℕ} (χ₁ : DirichletCharacter R n) (χ₂ : DirichletCharacter R m) : DirichletCharacter R (mul χ₁ χ₂).conductor
result.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] →
    {n m : ℕ} →
      (χ₁ : DirichletCharacter R n) → (χ₂ : DirichletCharacter R m) → DirichletCharacter R (χ₁.mul χ₂).conductor
result.informal_name: Primitive Dirichlet Character of the Product
result.informal_description: Given Dirichlet characters $\chi_1$ modulo $n$ and $\chi_2$ modulo $m$, the primitive Dirichlet character of their product $\chi_1 \cdot \chi_2$ is the unique character modulo the conductor $d$ of the product, defined by composing the product character with the canonical projection $\mathbb{Z}/\mathrm{lcm}(n,m)\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$.

name: DirichletCharacter
primitive_mul_isPrimitive
result.signature: {m : ℕ} (ψ : DirichletCharacter R m) : IsPrimitive (primitive_mul χ ψ)
result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] {n : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter R n) {m : ℕ}
  (ψ : DirichletCharacter R m), (χ.primitive_mul ψ).IsPrimitive
result.informal_name: The Primitive Character of the Product is Primitive
result.informal_description: For any Dirichlet characters $\chi$ modulo $n$ and $\psi$ modulo $m$, the primitive Dirichlet character of their product $\chi \cdot \psi$ is itself primitive, i.e., its conductor equals its modulus.

name: DirichletCharacter
conductor
result.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → DirichletCharacter R n → ℕ
result.informal_description: The conductor of a Dirichlet character $\chi$ is the infimum of the conductor set of $\chi$, which consists of all natural numbers $d$ such that $\chi$ factors through the projection from $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ to $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$, where $m$ is the modulus of $\chi$.

name: DirichletCharacter
conductorSet
result.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → DirichletCharacter R n → Set ℕ
result.informal_name: Conductor set of a Dirichlet character
result.informal_description: The set of natural numbers $ d $ for which the Dirichlet character $ \chi $ factors through the projection from $ \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z} $ to $ \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z} $, where $ m $ is the modulus of $ \chi $.

name: DirichletCharacter
conductor_ne_zero
result.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] {n : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter R n), n ≠ 0 → χ.conductor ≠ 0
result.value: := fun h ↦ hn <| Nat.eq_zero_of_zero_dvd <| h ▸ conductor_dvd_level _
result.informal_description: For a Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $n$ with $n \neq 0$, the conductor of $\chi$ is non-zero, i.e., $\operatorname{conductor}(\chi) \neq 0$.

name: DirichletCharacter
conductor_mem_conductorSet
result.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] {n : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter R n), χ.conductor ∈ χ.conductorSet
result.informal_name: Conductor of Dirichlet Character is in Conductor Set
result.informal_description: The conductor $ d $ of a Dirichlet character $ \chi $ is an element of its conductor set, i.e., $ d \in \text{conductorSet}(\chi) $.
